Thought: The potential energy of the system after minimization is given as -4119.6729 eV. To calculate the surface energy, I need to determine the energy difference between the bulk and surface configurations and divide by the surface area. The bulk energy is the same as the minimized energy since the simulation was set up to model the surface. The surface area can be calculated from the dimensions of the simulation box. The box dimensions are 27.21851 Å in the x and y directions, so the surface area is \(27.21851 \times 27.21851\) Å². The surface energy is then calculated as the energy difference per unit area.

Let's calculate the surface energy:

\[
\text{Surface Energy} = \frac{\text{Energy Difference}}{\text{Surface Area}} = \frac{-4119.6729 \, \text{eV}}{27.21851 \times 27.21851 \, \text{Å}^2}
\]

Calculating this gives:

\[
\text{Surface Energy} = \frac{-4119.6729}{740.851} \approx -5.56 \, \text{eV/Å}^2
\]
Final Answer: -5.56
